prompts.career.skills.short: Which skills should I list on a CV for [position], given that I've done: [experience]?
prompts.career.skills.detailed: Help me choose skills for my CV. Position: [position]. My experience: studies, projects, part-time work, volunteering: [experience]. Split the skills into job-specific and transferable. For each, say which part of my experience backs it up. Don't add skills my experience doesn't show. No contact or personal details needed.
prompts.career.skills.refine: Phrase the skills using the words job postings in this field usually use.
prompts.career.skills.check: Here's my skills list: [list]. Which one couldn't I back up with an example?
prompts.career.experience.short: Help me describe my experience honestly for a CV: [what I did]
prompts.career.experience.detailed: Help me describe experience for a CV. What I did: [what I did]. What came of it: [result]. Write 3–4 bullet points using “action — how — result”. Use only what I've written. If the result has no numbers, don't invent any; describe it qualitatively. Note which details you'd like me to clarify.
prompts.career.experience.refine: Here are the clarifications: [clarifications]. Update the bullet points.
prompts.career.experience.check: Does anything in these points sound exaggerated? [points]
prompts.career.portfolio.short: What should go in a portfolio for [field]?
prompts.career.portfolio.detailed: Help me plan a portfolio for [field]. My work: [work]. Pick the best 4–6 and explain why. For each: how to present it (task, my contribution, process, result), what to show visually. Suggest what's missing and what I could make in [time] to fill the gap.
prompts.career.portfolio.refine: In the team project [project], how do I honestly show my contribution?
prompts.career.portfolio.check: Here's the description of one piece: [description]. Is it clear what I did myself?
prompts.career.interview.short: What should I ask a professional in [field] to learn about the job?
prompts.career.interview.detailed: I want to talk to someone who works as a [profession] to see whether the field suits me. Write 12 questions: about a typical day, what they like and dislike, how they got into it, the skills needed, advice for a beginner. Add a short, polite message asking for a 20-minute chat.
prompts.career.interview.refine: Cut it to the 5 most important questions in case they're short on time.
prompts.career.interview.check: Here's what I learned: [notes]. What can I conclude and what should I still find out?
prompts.career.directions.detailed: I'm choosing between: [paths]. My interests: [interests]. Strong subjects: [subjects]. Table: what's taught, which subjects matter for admission, what the work involves, which skills develop, what I might dislike. Don't give specific salaries or university rankings. End with 5 questions I should ask myself.
prompts.career.directions.refine: How could I try each path out in practice before applying?
prompts.career.directions.check: I'm leaning towards [path]. Which of my answers point for and against?
prompts.career.grow.short: What skills should I build to grow in [field]?
prompts.career.grow.detailed: I [who I am: study, work] in [field], and currently can: [skills]. Goal in a year: [goal]. Suggest 5 skills to develop: why it matters, how I'll know I've got it, a first step. Mark which will have the quickest effect.
prompts.career.grow.refine: I have [hours] hours a week. Which 2 skills should I pick?
prompts.career.grow.check: How can I check my [skill] is at the level needed for [goal]?
prompts.career.learn.short: Make a plan to learn [skill] in [time].
prompts.career.learn.detailed: I want to learn [skill]. Current level: [level]. Time: [hours] hours a week for [time]. Make a week-by-week plan: what to learn, a practical task to do, how to check progress. Focus on practice. Instead of naming specific courses, describe types of resources and what to look for in them.
prompts.career.learn.refine: I'm stuck at week [number]. How else could I get through this stage?
prompts.career.learn.check: Give me a task that will show whether I've mastered the first stage.
prompts.career.letter.short: Help me write a cover letter for [job].
prompts.career.letter.detailed: Help with a cover letter. Job (key requirements): [requirements]. My relevant experience: [experience]. Why I'm interested: [motivation]. Structure: who I am and what I'm applying for, 2 examples of how my experience fits the requirements, why this company, availability to talk. Up to 200 words. No personal contact details in the text.
prompts.career.letter.refine: Make it simpler and livelier; remove generic phrases like “responsible and communicative”.
prompts.career.letter.check: If you removed the company name, would this letter fit any job? What could be more specific?
prompts.career.questions.short: What will I be asked in an interview for [position]?
prompts.career.questions.detailed: I have an interview for [position], level [level]. Write 10 likely questions: about me, motivation, experience, situational, technical. For each, say what they're looking for and which example from my experience I could use: [experience]. Add 3 questions I could ask them.
prompts.career.questions.refine: Run a mock interview: ask one question at a time and give feedback.
prompts.career.questions.check: My answer to “tell me about yourself”: [answer]. What should I cut or add?
prompts.career.vacancy.short: Break down this job posting: what's required and what matters? [posting]
prompts.career.vacancy.detailed: Break down the job posting. Table: requirement, required or nice-to-have, whether I have it (my experience: [experience]), how to show it on my CV or in the interview. Separately: what's unclear and worth asking about, and possible red flags (vague duties, requests to pay for training). Posting: [posting]
prompts.career.vacancy.refine: Where do I have gaps against the requirements? How could I close them in [time]?
prompts.career.vacancy.check: Should I apply if I meet about [percent]% of the requirements? What are the arguments for and against?

verify.career.skills: Only list skills on your CV that you can back up with an example. You'll be asked about them in interviews.
verify.career.experience: Don't exaggerate results. If you don't have numbers, it's better to describe the action honestly than invent a percentage.
verify.career.portfolio: Before publishing work, check you have the right to show it, especially for school or team projects.
verify.career.interview: Don't look up or paste people's personal contact details into the prompt. Reach out through official channels or mutual contacts.
verify.career.directions: Check admission requirements, fees and programmes on the institutions' official websites: they change every year.
verify.career.grow: Lists of “future skills” often follow trends. Compare with real job postings in your field.
verify.career.learn: Check specific courses and resources yourself: the AI may name outdated or non-existent ones.
verify.career.letter: The letter should sound like you. Employers recognise template text; keep your own wording.
verify.career.questions: Prepare answers using real examples from your own experience, not AI templates.
verify.career.vacancy: Confirm conditions, pay and requirements with the employer. The AI only sees the text you pasted.
